q: Records show a learner's self-injury coincides with recurrent ear infections. The functional analysis should therefore:
choices: A. Be postponed until the infections resolve permanently
B. Treat the infections as an unmeasurable confound
C. Replace the alone condition with a pain probe
D. Sample both symptomatic and symptom-free periods

q: A trial-based functional analysis and a standard analysis produce conflicting functions for the same student. The analyst should:
choices: A. Investigate the discrepancy and rely on the standard analysis
B. Report the behavior as multiply controlled by both functions
C. Adopt the trial-based result for its ecological validity
D. Average the two outcomes into a combined hypothesis

q: A single-operant reinforcer assessment answers which question about a stimulus?
choices: A. Does it function as a reinforcer at all
B. Which topography of responding does it occasion
C. How quickly will the client satiate on it
D. Is it preferred over the client's highest-ranked item
